reason: E2 supports the superiority of Al2O3 as an oxidation barrier at 1200°C, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that pack cementation aluminization works on refractory HEAs, that an aluminide layer will form a continuous adherent Al2O3 scale on these alloys, or that the untreated alloy oxidizes poorly under the stated conditions. The key mechanistic and material-specific premises are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Alumina (Al2O3) is a superior oxidation barrier with low oxygen diffusivity and high stability at 1200°C
Pack cementation can diffuse aluminum into refractory alloy surfaces to form an aluminide layer
The aluminide layer will oxidize to form a continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale during high-temperature air exposure
Refractory HEAs (e.g., Nb–Ta–W–Mo–V) lack inherent oxidation resistance and form thick, non-protective scales
Aluminization will significantly reduce oxidation rate compared to untreated alloy under the specified conditions
